AUDIT GPT-6.1 Sol — growth-project-backend#653 @ 9a23e3b2471794a1356d9939cc4e06682f1ea7ec — VERDICT: REQUEST CHANGES

AUD-SOL-SCHA-121, agent 121 — independent first full T4 request-expiry/schema/concurrency audit. A/B/C = 0/2/1.

The complete 1,437-line delta from the approved split top was read, including the enum/backfill/lease RLS migration and down script, expiry/lazy-expiry CAS, list/view/slot integration, notice claims/recovery and all tests; no other lens's current-round notes or verdict were read. [Exact candidate](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/653).

### B-653-1 — a move waiting on the coach lock can revive a request after its clear time

`src/scheduling/scheduling-session-lifecycle.service.ts:408,420-434,469-487` captures `now` before entering `runBookingTx`, then uses that pre-wait instant for the expiry checks, `requestStillOpen` predicate and the fresh response deadline. [Candidate](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/653).

Concrete counterexample: a client starts moving the still-open request at deadline minus one second, then obtains the coach advisory lock at deadline plus one second; the old timestamp still satisfies the deadline predicate, so the request moves and gains another response window instead of returning `409 REQUEST_EXPIRED`. [Independent boundary probe](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37366141725).

**Minimal fix rule:** after acquiring the relevant coach/session locks, reevaluate expiry against fresh time and enforce the deadline at the actual update boundary; audit the same clock-through-row-lock issue in the approve/decline/cancel CAS rather than trusting a JS timestamp bound before a blocking update. Database `now()` is transaction-start time, so use an actual post-wait clock/fence, not merely a different frozen timestamp.

**Verification:** replay the independent `a client move queued before its deadline...` case unchanged and require `409 REQUEST_EXPIRED` with the original interval retained; add an equivalent real-PostgreSQL deadline/row-lock race to the required live lane.

### B-653-2 — stale sweep-start leases allow duplicate notices after a long pass

`src/scheduling/jobs/request-expiry.job.ts:114-127,247-256,375-395` never renews/checks the four-minute singleton lease while processing its potentially long passes, and both fresh/taken-over notice leases use the original `sweep(now)` rather than the time the claim is made. [Candidate](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/653).

Concrete counterexample: the expiry pass consumes five minutes, then the first worker claims both notices with already-expired `lease_until = sweepStart+4m`; a second instance takes the expired singleton and those notice claims while the first is at its first delivery, and the unfenced old worker still delivers both recipients. [Independent boundary probe](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37366141725).

**Minimal fix rule:** start/renew each notice lease from the actual claim time, keep singleton ownership renewed and generation-fenced or stop work before losing it, and verify current claim ownership before emitting; stale same-instance release must not clear a newer acquisition. Bound/paginate the work while retaining catch-up and dead-worker recovery.

**Verification:** reproduce the independent long-pass/two-worker schedule, require at most one delivery per recipient, and retain the dead-worker takeover control; a stop-on-lost-ownership fix may adapt the probe's first-delivery barrier to permit that worker to finish without emitting. Cover slow/backlogged work plus two real PostgreSQL runners before next READY.

### C-653-1 — defense-in-depth log boundary

`src/scheduling/scheduling-session-lifecycle.service.ts:873` newly prints free-form `(err as Error).name` in the lazy-expiry audit catch; normal `AuditService.write` catches its failures already, making this a defensive follow-up rather than an ordinary-path blocker. [Candidate](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/653).

Follow-up rule: use the already available `safeLogDiagnostic(err)` and a synthetic unknown-name logger canary. Under the freeze this C is not required unless the same lines are changed for a B fix.

### Execution and integration

The independent three-case boundary spec was written and submitted alongside the existing expiry, lifecycle-integrity and delivery-status suites; its lane was still **queued, not executed**, when checked at 12:59 PDT on October 5. The two findings above are concrete code-derived counterexamples, not claimed executed failures. The third submitted case is a dead-worker-takeover control. No rerun or extra queue push was issued during the runner-assignment incident. [Submitted boundary lane](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/actions/runs/37366141725).

All required checks currently succeed at this unchanged PR head; green unit/ordinary live CI does not cover these delayed-deadline and expired-ownership schedules, and the PR's disclosed expiry-specific PostgreSQL enum/slot-release/lease coverage remains part of next-round acceptance. [Exact candidate](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-backend/pull/653).

No merge, deployment, PR-branch edit, production operation or local heavy command by this lens. Keep the owner's 48h/1h/30-minute answer rule and >24h quiet closure; the required changes preserve functionality, not remove expiry or recovery.
